Class Toggle

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.AbstractPanelElement<Toggle>
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.core.Toggle
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class Toggle extends AbstractPanelElement<Toggle>
A two-state on/off control. The general primitive for boolean setting interactions. Clicking flips the state and fires a callback with the new boolean value.

Renders using MenuKit's existing PanelStyle vocabulary rather than a custom toggle sprite:

  • Off: PanelStyle.RAISED background
  • On: PanelStyle.INSET background (visually "pressed in")
  • Hover (either state): translucent white highlight overlay
  • Disabled: PanelStyle.DARK background; no hover highlight; clicks are ignored

For a sprite-backed toggle, see sprite(int, int, int, int, boolean, Consumer, Identifier) — the on state renders the same sprite through MenuKit's HSL-lightness inversion pipeline, so consumers don't author two textures.

Toggle supports an optional label. A labeled Toggle renders as a bar that shows its label (raised = off, inset = on), auto-sized to fit the text — the label sits on the toggle body, so it is unmistakably the toggle's own, not text beside it. An unlabeled Toggle is the bare switch. For the conventional settings-checkbox visual (square + check-mark) instead, use Checkbox.

Mutable-state exception to the declared-structure discipline

MenuKit's declared-structure discipline says structure is frozen at construction and visibility is the only mutable dimension. Toggle is one of a narrow set of elements (alongside Checkbox and Radio) that owns mutable boolean state as a second mutable dimension.

The exception is legitimate because state changes do not affect structural shape — flipping a toggle does not add or remove elements, does not alter layout, and does not mutate the panel's element list. The only things that change are the internal boolean and the subsequent render pass. No downstream structural consequence.

Scope of the exception: Toggle, Checkbox, Radio. Does not extend to other elements. For state that lives outside the element (config files, block entities, player attachments), use the Phase 9 state-linked variant (see Toggle.linked(...)) which reads from a consumer-owned BooleanSupplier instead of owning state internally.

    • layoutWithin

      public void layoutWithin(int budget)
      Cap the labeled BAR to the panel's budget (reversible); a bare/sprite switch is intrinsic and ignores it, mirroring its fillWidth no-op.

      Beyond the width cap, this also resolves the label's WRAP: at the capped inner width (the bar's budget minus the L+R label inset) it asks the vanilla font splitter how many lines the label takes. If the label's natural single-line width exceeds that inner area it wraps (line count > 1) and getHeight() grows the bar to fit; if it fits, the count resets to 1 and the bar stays single-line. Recomputed every pass, so a later wider budget un-wraps it — fully reversible (mirrors TextLabel.layoutWithin).

      Parameters:
      budget - horizontal pixels available to this element, in panel content space. Always >= 1.

    • extraLayoutHeight

      public int extraLayoutHeight()
      Extra vertical pixels the WRAPPED bar occupies beyond its authored height — getHeight() - height when wrapped, else 0. The owning Panel reflows the elements below this toggle downward by exactly this amount, so a label that grows from one line to two pushes (never paints over) what's beneath it. Mirrors TextLabel.extraLayoutHeight.

    • fillWidth

      public void fillWidth(int width)
      Column-fill (Pass 3): stretch the LABELED bar form to the column's widest extent. A bare/sprite switch is intrinsically sized — stretching its track would distort it — so fillWidth is a no-op when there's no label (the same intrinsic-width principle Icon/Checkbox/Radio follow).
      Parameters:
      width - the column's widest-child extent to stretch to, in pixels

    • currentState

      protected boolean currentState()
      Returns the Toggle's current boolean state.

      Stable extension point for consumer Toggle subclasses. Override to read state from external storage (supplier, block entity, config file, etc.). The default implementation returns the element-owned internal state.

      Base Toggle's render and click handling call currentState() exactly once per frame. Subclasses overriding currentState() may rely on this: their supplier is invoked once per frame for base Toggle's rendering purposes. If the supplier returns different values across rapid successive calls, only the first call per frame affects the rendered output.

    • applyState

      protected void applyState(boolean newState)
      Commits a state transition. Subclasses define what "commit" means for their state-ownership model:
      • Base Toggle (element-owned state): writes the new state to internal storage and fires the onToggle callback with the new state.
      • Toggle.linked (consumer-owned state): fires the consumer's callback with the new state; consumer is responsible for updating their own state. No internal storage commit happens.

      Called from the toggleTo orchestration helper after the short-circuit no-op check passes. Implementations should be atomic — the state transition and the callback notification are conceptually a single event.

      Stable extension point. Signature and semantic contract maintained across MenuKit versions.

    • renderBackground

      protected void renderBackground(RenderContext ctx, int sx, int sy, boolean on, boolean disabled, boolean hovered)
      Paints the toggle's full visual — background and any state-dependent overlays. Called from render(RenderContext) after hover and on/off state have been resolved for the frame. Default implementation uses PanelStyle backgrounds (RAISED off, INSET on, DARK disabled) plus the translucent white hover highlight.

      Stable extension point for consumer Toggle subclasses. The signature (RenderContext, int sx, int sy, boolean on, boolean disabled, boolean hovered) and the semantic contract — sx/sy are the absolute screen-space top-left of the toggle; this hook owns ALL state-dependent painting (subclasses paint their own hover/disabled overlays) — are maintained across MenuKit versions. Consumer subclasses may rely on these properties.

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(double mouseX, double mouseY, int button)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Called when the mouse is clicked on this element. The dispatcher hit-tests against the element's bounds before calling this method, so implementations know the click is within bounds.

      Returns true if this element consumed the click (preventing further dispatch to slots or vanilla). The default returns false, so render-only elements (TextLabel, Icon, ItemDisplay) don't need to override it.

      The button parameter is the mouse button: 0=left, 1=right, 2=middle. Core Button only consumes left-click; custom elements can handle any button.

      Parameters:
      mouseX - screen-space mouse X
      mouseY - screen-space mouse Y
      button - mouse button (0=left, 1=right, 2=middle)
      Returns:
      true if consumed, false to let the click fall through

    • linked

      public static Toggle linked(int childX, int childY, int width, int height, BooleanSupplier state, Consumer<Boolean> onToggle)
      Creates a Toggle whose state lives in consumer code instead of inside the element. The consumer provides a BooleanSupplier that drives rendering each frame and a Consumer<Boolean> that fires with the new state when the user clicks to toggle.

      Persistence framing

      State persistence is a consumer concern. MenuKit does not ship a persistence abstraction — no PersistentValue<T>, no BooleanFlag, no config-backed state helpers. If you need a toggle whose state persists, use Toggle.linked and back the supplier and callback with wherever your state actually lives: a block entity, player attachment, config file, static field on a singleton, or anywhere else. The supplier reads; the callback signals. The library gives you the visual element and user input handling; the storage is yours to define.

      Self-healing behavior

      If the onToggle callback fails to update consumer state (bug, exception, swallowed error), the next frame's render reads the supplier and shows the unchanged state. The toggle visually snaps back to its pre-click appearance. State displayed is always state reported by the supplier — there is no internal state that could diverge from consumer state.

      Typical usage

      Toggle.linked(x, y, w, h,
    () -> config.autoSort,
    newState -> config.autoSort = newState);
      Parameters:
      childX - X position within panel content area
      childY - Y position within panel content area
      width - width in pixels
      height - height in pixels
      state - supplier invoked each frame to drive rendering
      onToggle - fired on user-initiated state changes, carrying the new state; consumer updates their own state store in response. Unified with the element-owned Toggle's Consumer<Boolean> callback shape.

    • sprite

      public static Toggle sprite(int childX, int childY, int width, int height, boolean initialState, Consumer<Boolean> onToggle, net.minecraft.resources.Identifier sprite)
      Creates a Toggle whose visual is a consumer-supplied sprite. The off state renders the sprite as-is; the on state renders the sprite through the HSL-lightness-inversion pipeline so the same sprite asset communicates both states without the consumer authoring a second "toggled" texture. Hue + saturation are preserved through the inversion; only the per-pixel lightness flips. Hover overlay applies on top of either state; disabled adds a dark overlay.

      Pairs with the static-state Toggle constructor — state is owned inside the element. For consumer-owned state, use the spriteLinked variant.

      Parameters:
      childX - X position within panel content area
      childY - Y position within panel content area
      width - toggle width in pixels (typically matches sprite width)
      height - toggle height in pixels (typically matches sprite height)
      initialState - starting boolean state
      onToggle - fired on each state change with the new state
      sprite - sprite identifier for both off and on states (on state is rendered through the HSL-inversion pipeline)

    • sprite

      public static Toggle sprite(int childX, int childY, int width, int height, boolean initialState, Consumer<Boolean> onToggle, Supplier<net.minecraft.resources.Identifier> sprite)
